title: Server DB, Registry, And State Import
objective: Make Server V2 the durable owner of OpenWork-managed state by introducing sqlite, canonical registry tables, and idempotent import from current desktop and orchestrator state.

steps.name: Define the server working directory layout
steps.description: Choose and implement the server-owned working directory layout for sqlite, managed config, runtime data, and workspace records so later phases do not invent conflicting filesystem paths.
successFactors: The chosen layout matches the direction in `schema.md` and `ideal-flow.md`.
Code can compute the working directory reliably in desktop-hosted and standalone modes.
The layout separates server-managed config from user data directories.

steps.name: Add sqlite bootstrap
steps.description: Introduce the sqlite dependency, connection setup, and startup bootstrap for the new server so it can persist OpenWork-owned metadata independently of the app.
successFactors: Server V2 can create or open its sqlite database on boot.
Connection lifetime and cleanup are explicit.
The DB path lives under server-owned storage, not app-local ad hoc files.

steps.name: Create the migration runner
steps.description: Add a migration system for schema creation and upgrades so later phases can evolve the DB safely instead of hand-editing bootstrap SQL.
successFactors: Migrations run automatically on startup or through a clear command.
Fresh boot and upgrade boot both work.
Migration state is tracked and reproducible.

steps.name: Create the `servers` table
steps.description: Add the canonical registry table for local and remote server connections, including hosting kind, base URL, capabilities, and token references or encrypted token material.
successFactors: The schema matches the intent in `schema.md`.
A local server record can be represented without hacks.
Remote and cloud-hosted servers can share one model with hosting metadata.

steps.name: Create the `workspaces` table
steps.description: Add the canonical workspace registry table, including local, remote, control, and help workspaces and the mapping fields needed for OpenCode or remote OpenWork backends.
successFactors: Every workspace points at exactly one server.
Local workspaces keep a stable OpenWork ID separate from OpenCode project IDs.
Remote workspace rows can store remote server mapping cleanly.

steps.name: Create server runtime state tables
steps.description: Add `server_runtime_state` and `workspace_runtime_state` or equivalent tables so runtime health, sync timestamps, and diagnostic metadata have a durable home.
successFactors: Server-level runtime data can be stored separately from workspace metadata.
Workspace-level diagnostics do not duplicate session source-of-truth data.
The schema can support OpenCode and router health in later phases.

steps.name: Create managed config item tables
steps.description: Add tables for MCPs, skills, plugins, and provider configs so OpenWork-managed product metadata moves out of app-local file mutation patterns.
successFactors: Each managed concept has a stable ID and metadata columns.
The schema preserves `source` or ownership metadata for imported versus managed items.
Later config projection work can read from these tables without schema changes.

steps.name: Create linking tables for workspace assignments
steps.description: Add workspace-to-config linking tables so config items can be attached to one or many workspaces and nothing is global by default.
successFactors: Workspace assignment is explicit instead of implied by file placement.
The schema supports attaching existing items during workspace creation.
Later phases can materialize effective workspace config from links plus items.

steps.name: Create cloud, share, and router tables
steps.description: Add `cloud_signin`, `workspace_shares`, `router_identities`, and `router_bindings` tables so later phases have durable server-owned homes for these product surfaces.
successFactors: Cloud auth metadata is no longer forced to remain app-only state.
Workspace share data can be stored as workspace-scoped access, not server-wide grants.
Router identities and bindings are modeled at the server level.

steps.name: Build repository and service layers over the schema
steps.description: Add typed repositories or service boundaries for CRUD and lookup operations so route code does not speak raw SQL directly.
successFactors: Registry logic is reusable across routes and bootstrap paths.
SQL access is encapsulated behind intention-revealing methods.
The service layer is testable without HTTP wiring.

steps.name: Seed the canonical local server record
steps.description: Ensure the local desktop-hosted or standalone server gets a canonical row in `servers` on startup so the registry model is real from day one.
successFactors: A fresh boot creates the local server record automatically.
Repeated boots do not create duplicate local server rows.
The local server row includes the correct hosting metadata and capability placeholders.

steps.name: Seed hidden control and help workspaces
steps.description: Create server-managed hidden workspaces for control and help behavior so the ideal model already exists in the registry even if the UI stays hidden for now.
successFactors: Control and help workspaces are real records with `is_hidden` semantics.
They do not appear in normal workspace lists by default.
They can still be addressed by dedicated future routes or UI flows.

steps.name: Define canonical workspace ID and slug generation
steps.description: Add the ID, slug, and display-name generation rules for workspace records so later phases can create and import workspaces without identity drift.
successFactors: Workspace IDs remain stable and independent from OpenCode project IDs.
Slug generation handles collisions predictably.
The chosen rules are reusable during import and new workspace creation.

steps.name: Import `openwork-workspaces.json` and desktop workspace state
steps.description: Build an importer that reads existing desktop workspace registry state and turns it into canonical server-owned `servers` and `workspaces` records.
successFactors: Existing local and remote workspaces can be reconstructed without hand edits.
Imported records preserve enough metadata for reconnect and migration.
The importer can be rerun without duplicating rows.

steps.name: Import remote workspace mapping and selection metadata
steps.description: Preserve current remote workspace mappings, selected-workspace metadata, and related desktop state that still matters for reconnect or migration into server-owned records.
successFactors: Remote workspace mappings survive migration.
Selection or reconnect hints move toward server ownership where appropriate.
The importer can safely skip purely transient UI state.

steps.name: Import cloud signin and auth metadata
steps.description: Move durable cloud base URL, auth token metadata, user/org data, and validation timestamps into `cloud_signin` or equivalent server-owned storage.
successFactors: Durable cloud settings stop being purely app-owned preference data.
Sensitive auth material has a defined storage model.
The server can use imported cloud metadata directly in later phases.

steps.name: Import orchestrator snapshots that still matter
steps.description: Read any remaining orchestrator state snapshots or auth files that are still needed for reconnect, runtime transition, or migration and normalize only the durable pieces into the server DB.
successFactors: Important reconnect metadata is preserved.
Ephemeral orchestrator-only state is not copied blindly into the new server model.
The import path leaves a visible record of what was imported versus ignored.

steps.name: Make startup import idempotent and observable
steps.description: Ensure import can run repeatedly without corruption and surfaces clear migration status, warnings, and failures instead of silently leaving split ownership behind.
successFactors: Running import twice does not create duplicate rows or drift state.
Migration failures are visible in logs or status output.
Recovery or retry behavior is possible without manual DB surgery.

steps.name: Add startup diagnostics for registry and migration state
steps.description: Expose enough startup diagnostics for developers and later agents to see whether the local server record, hidden workspaces, and imported state were created correctly.
successFactors: Logs or debug status make import outcomes explicit.
Developers can tell whether they are on a fresh boot or a migrated boot.
Diagnostics do not require manually querying the DB to understand basic state.

steps.name: Add DB and import tests
steps.description: Write tests for fresh schema creation, migration upgrades, idempotent import, partial/corrupt input handling, and hidden workspace seeding so the state model becomes trustworthy early.
successFactors: Fresh boot and migrated boot are both covered by tests.
Idempotency is enforced by automated checks.
Corrupt legacy inputs fail visibly instead of leaving silent split ownership.
